chunks: It was said to him (peace be upon him): If the door of a man's house were closed, and he were left in it, from where would his livelihood reach him?
And he replied (peace be upon him):

key_terms.بَابُ بَيْتِهِ: The door of his house (metaphor for means of access)

ai.seo_question: Where does livelihood (rizq) come from if physical means are blocked?
ai.summary: In this narration from Nahj al-Balagha, Imam Ali (AS) elucidates the metaphysical nature of rizq by addressing the common misconception that material means alone guarantee sustenance. He affirms that while physical efforts are necessary, the actual provision is divinely decreed and can arrive from unexpected sources, reinforcing the Shia concept of balancing tawakkul (trust in God) with taking means (asbab). This highlights the interplay between human agency and divine will, a central theme in Islamic theology regarding sustenance.
